Web design in Gilmer, TX ought to be done by somebody who knows where Ore City is and why October matters. Maurice Johnson grew up in Gilmer. He now runs Dominion Web Design Pro from Big Sandy, in the southern part of Upshur County, and builds websites for the kind of businesses he grew up around: feed stores, cafes, mechanics, salons and the shops on the square. Every page is written by hand, and you see a free demo of your site before you pay for anything.

Knowing a town does not make a website better on its own. It does mean you will not spend the first phone call explaining your customers to the person writing about them.

The week Gilmer is not a small town

Gilmer had 4,843 residents at the 2020 census. Then the East Texas Yamboree comes around in October and the courthouse square and city park fill with a crowd the town could never produce on its own. The festival was first held in October 1935, after a weevil quarantine on the county's sweet potato crop was lifted, as a fall celebration of the harvest. Apart from a break during World War II, it has come back every October since, with a queen's coronation and several days of events around the square.

Look at it as a business owner rather than a local. For a few days, thousands of people who do not live here are walking around with a phone, looking for somewhere to eat, somewhere to stay, something to buy, and somebody who can fix whatever just broke on the drive in. They do not know your business exists. If you do not show up when they search, that money goes to whoever does.

A Yamboree checklist for your website

  • Live and indexed by late summer, not the week of the festival. New pages take time to show up in search.
  • Festival hours posted plainly, plus any days you are closed.
  • Where you are in relation to the square, in words a visitor understands.
  • A phone number that dials with one tap, at the top of every page.
  • Your Google Business Profile matching the site exactly: name, hours, phone.

The other fifty-one weeks

The rest of the year, Gilmer is the seat of a rural county of 40,892 people, spread out across timber and farm country in the Pineywoods. Customers here drive to you, and they look you up before they get in the truck. A rancher in Harmony or a family in Union Grove is not going to make the trip on a guess.

Gilmer also sits on U.S. 271 within reach of Longview and Tyler, which cuts both ways. Your customers will drive to the bigger towns, and businesses from those towns show up in Gilmer searches without trying. The only real defense is a site that says clearly, on its own pages, that you are here and what you do.

Who we build for around Gilmer

Almost always the owner who also does the work. Trades and contractors, farm and feed supply, barbecue and cafes, salons and barbers, auto and small engine repair, land and property people, and the stores around the square that everybody local knows and nobody passing through can find.

The starting point is usually one of three. No website at all, just a Facebook page Google barely reads. A site someone built years ago with an old phone number and wrong hours. Or a rented platform where you never owned the domain and the site vanishes if you stop paying. All three are fixable, and none of them require you to learn anything.

For most Gilmer businesses the right answer is the $497 Starter site: five hand-written pages, a contact form that emails you every lead, Google Maps and your hours, and the search basics submitted to Google. If you serve the whole county and beyond, the $997 Pro site adds 10 city pages, one each for places like Big Sandy, Ore City, Pittsburg, Gladewater and Longview. Both are one-time prices, and the pricing page has the full list.

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Gilmer. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

What to gather before you ask for the demo

You do not need anything to get the demo itself; your business name and what you do are enough. When you decide to go ahead, the build moves fastest if you have a few things together. A list of every service you offer, in your own words, even if it is scribbled on a legal pad. The towns you will actually drive to. Your hours, including how they change in October or during deer season. Whatever photos you have of your work, your shop or your crew; phone photos are fine. And the login for your domain if you already own one, or the name you want if you do not.

That is usually it. Maurice turns those notes into pages, sends them over for you to read, and changes whatever does not sound like you. The Starter site goes live in 7 to 14 days, and the thing that holds it up is almost always waiting on photos.

Four reasons a Gilmer business would hire Dominion Web Design Pro

1. He is from here

Maurice grew up in Gilmer. You will not have to explain the Yamboree, the square, or which way Ore City is.

2. The work comes before the bill

The demo site is built first. You look at it on your phone, show it around, and decide. If you pass, you owe nothing.

3. Small-town prices, one time

4. Honest about search

Free help for Upshur County businesses

The UT Tyler-Longview Small Business Development Center serves Upshur County along with Gregg, Harrison, Marion, Panola and Rusk, and its advising costs nothing. If you are writing a business plan or applying for a loan, start there. The Gilmer Area Chamber of Commerce is the local network, and in a town this size the referrals still count for a lot. We have no arrangement with either. They are simply the right first calls, and plenty of owners here have never made them.

Common questions

Who builds websites for small businesses in Gilmer, Texas?

Dominion Web Design Pro does, from Big Sandy in the same county. Maurice Johnson grew up in Gilmer and writes each page himself. You get a free demo of your site before you are asked to buy anything.

Is it worth having a website for a business this small?

Sometimes not yet. If you are booked solid off word of mouth and turning work away, a website is not your most urgent problem. It becomes one when referrals slow down, and a new site takes time to start showing up in searches. That is why the best time to build one is while you are still busy.

How do I get my Gilmer business found by Yamboree visitors?

Have a site that is live, accurate and indexed well before October, with your festival hours on it, your location relative to the square, and a phone number that taps to call. Pair it with a filled-in Google Business Profile. Visitors search on their phones while they are walking around, so the site has to load fast and say the basics in a few seconds.

What does a website cost for an Upshur County business?

The Starter site is $497 one time for five pages. Pro is $997 and adds 10 city pages for towns like Big Sandy, Ore City and Longview. Agency is $1,997. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included if you keep the AI agent.

Do you have an office in Gilmer?

No. Maurice works from Big Sandy and does the work by phone, link and email. He knows Gilmer because he grew up there, not because there is a storefront on the square.
